requirement: The review prompt MUST tell the reviewer that a report with only wording changes means it has not looked hard enough for gaps and conflicts. If the reviewer looks again and still finds no design questions, the prompt MUST direct it to say so explicitly.
rationale:
The requirement has two obligations for the review prompt. (1) The prompt MUST tell the reviewer that a report with only wording changes means it has not looked hard enough for gaps and conflicts. (2) If the reviewer looks again and still finds no design questions, the prompt MUST direct it to say so explicitly.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_rejects_a_report_with_only_wording_changes]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It reads the real prompt through `review_prompt()`, which loads `references/review-prompt.md` of the `habeas-requirements` skill. It takes the `## Report` section with `section`. It then calls `assert_text_in_order`, which panics if any phrase is missing or out of order. The phrases are:
- "A report with only wording changes means you have not looked hard enough for gaps and for conflicts" covers obligation 1, including both gaps and conflicts.
- "Look again" covers the looking-again step.
- "If you still find no design questions, write \"No design questions.\"" covers obligation 2, the explicit statement.

The ordered check also confirms the escalation sequence: the warning, then looking again, then the explicit statement.

The requirement has no further conditions, modes or boundaries to test. The assertions are on the prompt text, which is the only artifact the requirement governs, so they enforce its obligations. I found no gaps.
